claims.text: A data-driven or machine-learning model using phonon dispersion curve analysis can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed approach applies to high-entropy alloys in an initial, unprocessed state.
The model uses phonon dispersion curve analysis to predict phonon thermal conductivity.
Phonon dispersion curves describe lattice dynamics.
Phonon dispersion curves are related to thermal conductivity.
The relationship between phonon frequencies and thermal conductivity enables prediction of phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed model will improve prediction accuracy relative to current predictions.
Use of the predictive approach could produce a 10–20% reduction in thermal conductivity.
Current predictions of low phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys are inaccurate.
The approach is limited to high-entropy alloys used in thermal-insulation applications.
The relationship between phonon dispersion curves and thermal conductivity is well established within the stated applicability domain.
The approach is falsified if it fails to improve prediction accuracy by more than 5% over current predictions for at least 80% of tested high-entropy alloys.

contradictions.description: The intervention is only a predictive model, but the predicted outcome includes a 10–20% reduction in the material's thermal conductivity. A prediction method can improve identification or prediction error but does not itself physically reduce conductivity.
